newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran slams Rifkind Mideast plan as "colonialist".
newsitem.headline: Iran slams Rifkind Mideast plan as "colonialist".

text.p: Iran on Thursday blasted a British proposal to set up a body to help reduce conflict in the Middle East, saying the idea smacked of colonialism.

"Security in the Middle East and cooperation between this region's countries is no business of Britain's foreign minister," said Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati, quoted by state-run Tehran radio.

British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind proposed in Abu Dhabi on Monday a body along the lines of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) to encourage investment and regional cooperation.

"This country should know that the age of British colonialism...is over and that the people of this region know best what is in their interest and they do not need foreign guardians to cooperate," Velayati said.

Rifkind said the new organisation could include Turkey, and would eventually be open to countries like Iraq and Iran. He had a favourable response when he floated the idea with other regional countries and allies like the United States.
Iran said on Tuesday remarks by Rifkind on alleged Iranian links to terrorism made it difficult to normalise relations between the two countries.

Ties have been particularly strained since a 1989 death edict by late spiritual leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini against British writer Salman Rushdie for allegedly blaspheming Islam in his book "The Satanic Verses".

Britain says Iran should cancel the death order if it wants relations between the countries upgraded. Iranian officials say the edict cannot be revoked, but Iran would not send agents to kill Rushdie.
